enonce.texte:
Analyze the following asynchronous message. Identify at least three issues with it, and then rewrite it to be more effective.

Subject: Meeting

Hi all,

We need to have a meeting about the project. Can you let me know when you are available? Let me know if you have any questions.

Thanks,

Jane

questions.texte: Identify at least three issues with the message above.

sousQuestions.reponse: 1. Vague subject line ('Meeting' doesn't give any context). 2. No purpose or agenda provided. 3. No timeline or deadline for responses. 4. No proposed time slots, making it harder for people to coordinate. 5. 'Let me know if you have questions' is generic and doesn't encourage engagement.

sousQuestions.texte: Rewrite the message to be more effective.
sousQuestions.reponse:
Sample Answer:

Subject: Scheduling Project Sync Meeting - Please Complete Doodle Poll

Hi team,

We need to hold a 30-minute sync meeting to discuss the Q3 project milestones and the upcoming sprint planning.

Please complete this Doodle poll by Friday 5 PM to indicate your availability for next week: [link].

I'll send the meeting agenda and materials by Monday morning.

If the proposed times don't work for you, please let me know directly.

Thank you,

Jane

enonce.texte: Read the statements about video conference etiquette and identify whether each is True or False.

questions.texte: Evaluate the following statements about video conference participation.

sousQuestions.texte: It is acceptable to multitask (check emails, work on other tasks) during a video conference, as long as you are listening.
sousQuestions.reponse: False. Multitasking is disrespectful to the speaker and other participants. It can also cause you to miss important information.

sousQuestions.texte: You should always mute your microphone when you are not speaking.
sousQuestions.reponse: True. Muting your microphone prevents background noise from distracting others.

sousQuestions.texte: Using the chat feature to ask questions or share resources is acceptable during a presentation.
sousQuestions.reponse: True. The chat feature is a great way to ask questions without interrupting the speaker, or to share links and resources.

enonce.texte: You are the lead on a distributed team. You need to communicate a significant change in the project requirements. Write an asynchronous message (email or Slack/Teams) that clearly conveys the change, its impact, and next steps.

questions.texte: Write a clear async message to your team.

sousQuestions.texte: Write the message. Include: a clear subject/header, the reason for the change, the impact on the current work, the new timeline, and clear next steps.
sousQuestions.reponse:
Sample Answer (Email):

Subject: Important: Change in Project Requirements - Authentication Module

Hi team,

I hope this message finds you well.

I wanted to inform you about an important change in the project requirements. The client has requested that we add two-factor authentication (2FA) to the login system. This decision was made following a security audit they conducted.

Impact on Current Work:

  • We need to update the authentication module to support 2FA.
  • The timeline for the authentication milestone will be extended by 1 week.
  • No other modules are affected at this time.

New Timeline:

  • Authentication module completion: May 15 (extended from May 8).

Next Steps:

  • David: Please research 2FA libraries that integrate with our current stack. Share your findings by Tuesday.
  • Sarah: Please update the API documentation to include 2FA endpoints. Start on Wednesday.
  • All: Please join a quick sync meeting tomorrow at 10 AM to discuss implementation details. I'll send an invite.

Please review this change and let me know if you have any questions or concerns. I'm available on Slack for any immediate questions.

Thank you,

[Your Name]

enonce.texte: You have just participated in a video conference that was not very effective. Identify the problems and propose solutions for future meetings.

questions.texte: Analyze the video conference issues and propose solutions.

sousQuestions.texte:
Meeting Description:

The meeting lasted 1.5 hours. The agenda was not shared beforehand. Several participants had technical issues (audio cutting out, camera not working). The speaker shared their screen but the text was too small to read. One participant dominated the conversation. There were no clear action items or next steps at the end.
sousQuestions.reponse:
Problems:

  • No agenda shared → participants were unprepared.
  • Technical issues → wasted time and lost information.
  • Screen text too small → participants couldn't follow.
  • One person dominated → others didn't get to contribute.
  • No action items → meeting lacked purpose.

Solutions:

  • Always share an agenda 24 hours in advance.
  • Ask participants to test their audio and video before the meeting.
  • When sharing a screen, zoom in or adjust font size so text is readable.
  • Use a facilitator to ensure everyone has a chance to speak.
  • Always summarize decisions and action items at the end of the meeting.

enonce.texte: You are leading a new project with a team of 8 people distributed across 3 time zones. Create a remote communication plan that addresses: communication channels, meeting frequency, async communication practices, and documentation.

questions.texte: Create a comprehensive remote communication plan.

sousQuestions.texte: Write the plan with clear sections.
sousQuestions.reponse:
Sample Answer:

Remote Communication Plan - Project Alpha

1. Communication Channels:

  • Slack: For daily updates, quick questions, and informal communication.
  • Email: For formal communication, decisions, and documentation that needs a permanent record.
  • Zoom: For video conferences, meetings, and presentations.
  • Jira: For project tracking, task assignments, and progress updates.

2. Meeting Schedule:

  • Daily Stand-up (15 min): Every day at 10 AM GMT. Asynchronous for those who cannot attend (via Slack thread).
  • Sprint Planning (1 hour): Every Monday at 2 PM GMT.
  • Progress Review (30 min): Every Thursday at 3 PM GMT.
  • All meetings will be recorded for those who cannot attend.

3. Async Communication Practices:

  • All decisions and action items will be documented in a shared Google Doc.
  • Use @mentions and threads in Slack to keep discussions organized.
  • Respond to messages within 24 hours.
  • Use clear subject lines in emails.

4. Documentation:

  • Meeting notes will be posted in Confluence within 24 hours.
  • Project decisions will be documented in ADRs (Architecture Decision Records).
  • All documentation will be stored in the shared Google Drive folder.
